name: Personalised news feeds
title: Why PointCast failed, and when personalised feeds became viable
question: Why did PointCast fail, and when did personalised feeds become viable?
answer: PointCast (1992) pushed personalised news to desktop screens from 1996, reportedly turned down a $450M offer from News Corp in 1997, and was sold for a small fraction of that in 1999. Its constant updates clogged dial-up lines and office networks. Facebook's News Feed (2006) ran on always-on broadband, which had passed 20 lines per 100 Americans.
verdict_reason: Always-on broadband (about 20 per 100 in 2006) made a constantly updating feed cheap to deliver.

constraint.name: Always-on broadband
constraint.detail: A feed that updates all day needs a connection that is always on and not metered by the minute.

crossing.text: US fixed broadband reaches about 20 lines per 100 people (World Bank).
